title: Gen-BX
fill_note: DENSE layered wind with a jig; scorer cap 0.65
fill_how: The scored turns assume a dense, layer-by-layer wind at fill 0.65 (insulated-wire area / window; the scorer cap). Use a winding jig on a drill/lathe with a turn counter, lay each layer side-by-side with light back-tension, and do not scramble-wind: a scramble wind only reaches ≈0.55–0.60 and then the window holds fewer turns (scorer what-if `--fill 0.60` is in the table above). Never wind more than the listed turns — the copper must stay below the flanges.
steel_extra: **New steel:** Ø168 discs, M3 clamp map R30 at 0/90/180/270° and R44 on the inter-pole angles 67.5/112.5/247.5/292.5° (both inside the R71 magnet ring). Cut from this kit's `steel_backiron_disc.dxf`; no earlier disc fits.
o5_note: scan t6: diametric Ø5 assists lower this 8p/12c layout, so all 48 Ø5 are left out
card_title: Gen-BX · dual-rotor 8p/12c R71 THIN-COPPER big ring · bar bearing bridges
card_sub: 12 bobbins r53–88 × 6.75 mm copper (gap 9.35 mm) · poles R71 · no Ø5 · Ø168 steel · --back-iron · 2026-10-11
idea: Gap reduction paid for by a bigger ring: the Gen-BU 8p/12c layout with the copper cut from 8.1 to 6.75 mm (magnet face to magnet face 10.70 → 9.35 mm, so Bz at the copper rises) and the lost window area won back radially, with the poles moved out to R71 and the bobbins stretched to r53–88. The scans show the thin-copper optimum only appears on the bigger ring (on R66 it gains far less), and R71 / Ø194 stator is the largest machine that still packs on one 410 mm plate.
